title: I Love My Family
learningOutcomes: Introduce family members using complete sentences.
Identify the formation, sound, and words that begin with the letters Nn, Pp, Hh, and Dd.
Recognize numbers 1 to 5 and match them with their correct values.
Ask and answer number-related questions about people and objects.
Trace letters Nn, Pp, Hh, and Dd in their uppercase and lowercase forms.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Who is this? (Maya points to a picture)

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: This is my father. And this is my mother. They are my parents.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Oh, nice! Do you have any brothers?

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Can you show me their pictures?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Sure, I will show you pictures of my whole family.

activities.instruction: Listen, point, and write a check next to the matching picture.
Listen, look at the picture, then circle the correct family word.
Match the picture with the correct word.
Look at the picture, listen, then choose the correct answer.
Trace letter Nn in its uppercase and lowercase forms.
Circle the objects that start with the letter Nn.
Trace letter Pp in its uppercase and lowercase forms.
Circle the objects that start with the letter Pp.
Look at each picture, name it, then trace.
Look at the picture, then circle the beginning letter.

lessons.title: Numbers from 1 to 5

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: How many books do you have?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Aly, look! I have 5 apples. Do you want one?

lines.speaker: Aly
lines.text: Yes, please! I have 1 apple now. Thank you!

languagePatterns: How many books do you have?

activities.instruction: Listen to the teacher, point, and count.
Count, circle the correct number, then match.
Count the objects and match them with the correct number.
Look at each picture, count the objects, then circle.
Trace the numbers 1–5.
Trace letter Hh in its uppercase and lowercase forms.
Look at the picture, then circle the beginning letter.
Listen to your teacher and repeat the Dd words.
Trace letter Dd in its uppercase and lowercase forms.
Look, say, then circle the pictures that start with letter Dd.

vocabularyPolicyNote: 32 source-listed words and number words were extracted. No supplementary words were added. Family vocabulary, phonics examples and number words are grouped under their actual lesson sources.

grammar.note: The unit presents family identification patterns, have/has-style expressions in dialogue, there is/there are, and How many questions as language patterns. These have not been expanded into unsupported grammar rules.

reading.note: The two printed dialogues are the source texts for listening and speaking. No separate reading passage with comprehension questions was identified in the reviewed unit pages.

listening.note: The student book prints two dialogues and multiple listen-and-repeat or picture-choice tasks. Teacher-led exercises do not include a complete separate recording script.

assessment.note: Most tasks depend on pictures or teacher audio. They are recorded as source activities; no unseen image key or extra question set has been invented.
